title: The Library Card
author: Barashada Ingiriisiga
description: Fatima, new to the city, finds a warm place full of stories and screens. With a small library card, she opens big doors for herself and her son, learning that help is free and hope is a page away.

chapters.title: The Big Building
chapters.text:
Fatima walked past the big building every day. She took her son, Omar, to the shop. She went to the bus stop. She walked to the market. And every day, she passed the library.

The library was a tall, old building. It had big windows and white walls. Fatima looked at it but she never went inside. She did not know what was in there. She thought libraries were for other people. For students. For people who had time.

But today was different. Today was very cold. The wind was strong and the rain started to fall. Fatima held Omar's hand. Omar was three years old. He was crying because his hands were cold.

"Come on, Omar," Fatima said. "We can wait here."

She opened the big door and went inside. It was warm. It was quiet. And it was beautiful.

A woman smiled at her. The woman had grey hair and kind eyes. She wore a blue shirt with a name tag. It said "Mrs. Hall".

"Hello," the woman said. "Welcome to the library. Are you looking for something?"

Fatima felt shy. She looked at the floor. "No," she said. "It is cold outside. We just want to warm up."

"That is fine," Mrs. Hall said. "You can stay as long as you want. Would you like to see the children's corner?"

Fatima did not know what to say. She looked at Omar. Omar was looking at the big room. His eyes were wide.

"Come," Mrs. Hall said. "I will show you."

They walked past tall shelves full of books. Omar touched the books with his small hands. Then they came to a special room. It was full of colours. There were small chairs and small tables. There were picture books on low shelves. There was a big rug on the floor.

"Omar can play here," Mrs. Hall said. "And we have story time every Tuesday. A lady reads stories to the children."

Omar sat on the rug. He picked up a book with a red bus on the cover. He smiled.

Then Mrs. Hall showed Fatima the computers. "You can use these for free," she said. "You can read the news. You can write emails. You can learn new things."

Fatima looked at the computers. She did not know how to use them. But she wanted to learn.

Then the story time began. A young woman sat in a big chair. Children sat around her. Omar sat with them. The woman opened a book and started to read.

"Once there was a little duck who wanted to find a friend..."

Omar laughed. He laughed a big, happy laugh. Fatima heard him. She looked at her son's face. He was happy. He was warm. He was safe.

Fatima smiled. It was a small smile, but it was real.

Mrs. Hall came back. "Would you like a library card?" she asked. "It is free. You can borrow books. You can use the computers."

Fatima thought for a moment. Then she said, "Yes. Yes, I would like that."

chapters.title: My Own Card
chapters.text:
The next day, Fatima came back to the library with her son. She felt happier now. The library was warm and bright, and the people were very kind. She wanted a library card like the woman at the desk had said.

She walked up to the desk. A young man with glasses asked, "Can I help you?"

Fatima spoke slowly. She was a little shy. "I would like a library card," she said. "How can I get one?"

The man smiled. "That is easy," he said. "You need two things. One is an ID, and one is a piece of mail."

An ID? Fatima did not understand. The man saw her face. He explained again. "An ID is a card with your name and your picture. Like a card from your government or your workplace. And a piece of mail, like a letter or a bill that comes to your house."

"Ah, yes," Fatima said. She had an ID card from her country. She still had it in her bag. And she sometimes got letters from her brother. She had one in her home.

"Bring those things tomorrow," the man said. "Then you can fill in a form, and you will get your card. Your son can come too. There is a story time for children at ten o'clock."

The next day, Fatima put her ID and a letter in her bag. She walked to the library with her son. Her heart beat a little fast. But she felt ready.

The same young man was at the desk. Fatima gave him her two papers. They were the ID card with her picture and a letter. The man looked at them and said, "Very nice, part."

Then he gave her a white form. It was short. Fatima wrote her name, her address, and her phone number. She wrote a small, clear letters. The man took the form and said, "Wait one minute, please."

He came back with a blue card. "This is your card," he said. He held it out. Fatima took it. The card was blue and white. It had her name: Fatima. It felt in her hand. The librarian showed her how to use it.

"Now you can borrow books from the library. You can take them home for three weeks. Then you bring them back. If you finish a book and you want it, you can get another one too, here at this machine."

The man showed her a small computer at the side of the desk. It had a scanner. He put the blue card under the red light. *Beep!* Then he put the book under the light. *Beep!* "Now this book is yours for three weeks," he said.

Then he showed her the computers in the corner. "You can write emails. You can write letters here and print them," he said. Fatima touched the keyboard with her finger. It was very different from a pen . He showed her how to open a program and write her name.

Fatima smiled. She had her own card and a new way to use a library. It was a good day.

chapters.title: A New Door
chapters.text:
The next week, Fatima came back to the library. She smiled at the kind woman at the desk. She knew where to go now. She took her son to the children's corner first. He played with the toys and looked at the picture books. Then Fatima walked to the computers. She sat down and looked at the screen. It was not hard now. She remembered what the librarian had shown her.

She wanted to find a job. A man at the desk helped her. He said, "You can search for jobs on the computer." He showed her a website. Fatima typed her city and the word "job". Many names came up. She read them slowly. Some jobs were for cleaning, some for cooking, some for helping in shops. Fatima wrote down the ones she liked. She felt happy. She could do this.

The man also showed her how to print a form. "You need to fill this form for a job," he said. He pressed a button, and the paper came out of a big machine. Fatima watched. It was like magic. She took the paper and put it in her bag. She would fill it at home.

Her son came to her. He was a little bored. Fatima had an idea. She asked the librarian, "Can I read a story on the computer?" The librarian smiled. "Yes, of course. There are many stories online." She helped Fatima find a simple story about a cat. Fatima read the words on the screen. Her son sat on her lap and listened. He laughed when the cat fell down. Fatima read the story again. Her son loved it. She felt proud.

Every week, Fatima came back. She learned more. She could search for anything now. She could print forms for school, for the doctor, for the bank. She felt strong and smart.

One day, a new woman came in. She looked shy, like Fatima had been. She held a small baby and looked around. Fatima saw her and smiled. She walked to her and said, "Hello. Are you new here?" The woman nodded. "I am looking for the children's room," she said softly. Fatima said, "Come with me. I will show you." She took the woman to the children's corner. The woman said, "Thank you." Fatima felt warm inside. She was not a new person anymore. She was at home. The library was her place, and she could help others find it too.
